tasks.short: Organize support groups and counsel family members

steps.what: Organize support groups and family meetings with appropriate consent and access arrangements
Counsel family members or facilitate support groups to help them support the patient

tasks.design: Use native recurring meeting fields in {CALENDAR}, with permitted contact details checked in the {OTHER} care record, to reduce repeated logistics messages. The worker approves each exact invitation and retains consent discussions, group suitability and all counselling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Arrangements repeat the same time, location and access details across messages.
tasks.enabler_now: Native meeting templates can reuse approved logistics without selecting participants or generating counselling.
tasks.still_hard: Consent, family relationships and participant suitability need careful conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The worker responds to distress, conflicting perspectives and the family's understanding of the illness.
tasks.altitude: Keep support time intact while reducing a small amount of repeated meeting administration.

reach.task: Confirm accessible arrangements and contact permissions for family support
reach.learn: Respect confidentiality across patient and family relationships

evidence.claim: Native logistics templates can reduce repeated meeting entry; this is an E1 scenario, with no counselling saving implied.

assumptions: Boundary includes support meeting arrangements and counselling, not a separate case-note drafting task.

The worker produces participant identity, permitted contact, consent scope, suitability, date/time, venue and access instructions in s1. Its 20 remaining hours include all elicitation, capture, privacy checks and invitation approval; no structured group eligibility flag is assumed.
a1 follows assembly of the final invitation and binds recipients, contact route and logistics; any change voids it. Sensitive details and recipient lists are not exposed to other participants.
Use native recurring fields first. Missing permissions or unusual arrangements stay manual; existing template use earns no saving.
research_questions: Can templates reduce entry time after consent and recipient checks without exposing participant identities?

already_counted.description: Suitability, consent, logistics capture and invitation approval

incremental.description: Maintain invitation fields and access settings

approvals.approved_version: Exact invitation version, individually permitted recipients, contact route, meeting time, venue and access details; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+75=95; gross 5%, less 1 upkeep gives net 4%. Low 0 for already reused messages or extra consent coordination; counselling time stays intact.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Modify treatment plans when client status changes

steps.what: Review changes in client status with the client and relevant care professionals
Modify treatment plans through agreed professional decisions responding to changed client status
Record agreed treatment-plan changes and verify the revised internal version

tasks.design: Use versioned plan sections in the {OTHER} care record to retain unchanged facts and record the worker's agreed amendments once. The worker performs the assessment and plan decisions, then checks every changed and carried-forward section before saving; no treatment option is generated or selected automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: A limited plan change can require re-entering unchanged administrative sections.
tasks.enabler_now: Native plan versioning and explicit field reuse can remove retyping without interpreting client status.
tasks.still_hard: A status change may alter risk, goals and service coordination in ways that need discussion.
tasks.human_edge: The worker connects changed circumstances to practical support and the client's wishes.
tasks.altitude: Preserve time for plan judgement while reducing repeated documentation.

reach.task: Confirm responsibilities and feasibility of the agreed plan changes
reach.learn: Local decision authority and interdependent care actions

evidence.claim: Versioned field reuse may reduce unchanged-section entry; this is an E1 scenario and does not establish treatment-planning automation.

assumptions: Boundary is status review, plan modification and internal documentation; ongoing counselling, original assessment reports and delivery of revised care are separate. Other clinicians' labour is unchanged.

The worker produces verified change facts in s1 and the exact agreed amendments, owners and review arrangements in s2, retaining all 80 hours. No structured status-change, risk or eligibility score is supplied for free.

s3's ten remaining hours include amendment entry, checks of carried-forward content, version comparison and manual correction. Unclear decisions return to the responsible professional; no plan content is inferred.

Test native plan versions first. If the record already supports single-entry amendments there is no new saving. Local authority determines which changes the social worker may make; the task statement grants no additional clinical authority.
unknowns: Current re-entry burden and versioning features
research_questions: Does native amendment entry avoid retyping without retaining stale goals or responsibilities?

already_counted.description: Client-status review and professional plan decisions
Amendment capture and final version checks

incremental.description: Maintain plan fields and version-check guidance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=40+40+10=90; gross 10%, less 2 upkeep gives net 8%. Low 0 for existing amendment workflows or complete plan rewrites. No assessment or decision time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise workers providing client and patient services

steps.what: Review active service cases and assemble information for worker supervision
Supervise and direct workers providing services to clients or patients

tasks.design: Configure a native case-action view in {OTHER} and keep the supervision agenda in {DOCS}. It retrieves existing actions and evidence; the worker still reviews context and directly supervises colleagues, with no staff scoring or automated allocation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision preparation repeats navigation through existing case actions and records.
tasks.enabler_now: A native filtered view can reduce navigation while preserving source links.
tasks.still_hard: Context, professional uncertainty and staff support cannot be inferred from completion fields.
tasks.human_edge: The social worker gives constructive direction and recognizes when a colleague needs support or escalation.
tasks.altitude: Arrive with accessible case evidence while preserving supervision time and judgement.

reach.task: Coordinate escalation when supervision identifies unsafe or infeasible service arrangements
reach.learn: Support responsibilities and professional escalation routes

evidence.claim: A native case-action view can reduce repeated navigation; this is an E1 design with no measured supervision saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes supervision preparation and direct worker guidance, not original case recording, routine treatment delivery or formal personnel evaluation.

Case workers already produce dated actions, owners, status and source references in normal case recording. s1's 20 remaining hours include checking these records, capturing the specific supervision question and resolving missing information; no new staff reporting is required.
The view presents recorded facts without deriving risk, worker performance or case priorities. s2 retains all 75 hours for discussion and direction; urgent issues follow existing direct escalation.
Use native views before custom code. If current records cannot support a reliable view, prepare manually. Consultation and access review are included where a changed view affects staff-data use.
unknowns: Existing case-action completeness and native views
research_questions: Can supervisors retrieve relevant facts with less navigation and no extra case-worker entry?

already_counted.description: Case review, question capture and missing-information checks

incremental.description: Maintain view filters, source links and access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=20+75=95; gross 5%, less 2 upkeep gives net 3%. Low 0 for existing views or poor action records; live supervision is unchanged.

tasks.short: Plan and conduct community health and social-support programs

steps.what: Identify community health or social problems with participants and local service partners
Plan programs to address the agreed problems using appropriate interventions
Assemble program logistics, activity checklists and resource schedules
Conduct programs and respond to participant needs and emerging concerns

tasks.design: Keep community needs work and intervention design human, then reuse logistics templates in {PROJECT}, {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}. The worker checks the delivery pack and conducts the program; no generated intervention or automated service eligibility is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Program arrangements repeat resource lists, session fields and delivery checklists.
tasks.enabler_now: Native project templates can organize an agreed design without choosing a health intervention.
tasks.still_hard: Community trust, cultural fit and practical participation barriers require local work.
tasks.human_edge: The worker builds a program with people and adapts it to real responses.
tasks.altitude: Reduce logistical assembly while keeping needs assessment and program delivery accountable.

reach.task: Confirm local delivery resources and appropriate intervention guidance
reach.learn: Evidence quality and practical access constraints

evidence.claim: Reusable logistics templates may reduce program pack assembly; the estimate is E1, with no claim about health outcomes.

assumptions: Boundary includes program needs work, design, logistics and direct delivery; separate individual treatment plans and case-report writing are excluded.

The worker produces the program objective, intended participants, agreed approach and resource requirements in s1 and s2 with all 60 hours retained. No structured community need or intervention choice is supplied for free.

s3's 12 remaining hours include capture and checking of session dates, resource quantities, venue, responsible contacts and access requirements against the agreed design. Missing resource facts are resolved manually with the existing partners; no new partner reporting duty is introduced.
Use native templates first; unique programs and existing template users may gain nothing. All actual community engagement and delivery time remains.
unknowns: Current project templates and resource constraints
research_questions: Can a reused delivery pack reduce preparation without overlooking local access or resource needs?

already_counted.description: Community needs work and program design
Logistics capture, resource checking and pack review

incremental.description: Maintain program logistics templates and access

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=35+25+12+20=92; gross 8%, less 2 upkeep gives net 6%. Low 0 for unique programs or existing template use. No community engagement or delivery time is removed.

role.altitude: Keep counselling, plan judgement and supervision human while reducing limited repeated logistics and record entry.
reach: Coordinate care-plan responsibilities with care teams
Work with community partners on feasible program delivery
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who has dependable supporting records and protected attention for clients, families and colleagues.
